handbookNote: Nevada Department of Wildlife (NDOW) boating safety and education program (ndow.org) and Nevada Revised Statutes Chapter 488 (Watercraft) -- Nevada has NO single official state-administered boating knowledge exam; NRS 488.730 requires a person born on or after January 1, 1983 who will operate a power-driven vessel with a motor exceeding 15 horsepower to complete an approved safe-boating course or pass a proficiency exam, and NRS 488.740/488.750 have NDOW certify third-party course providers and maintain a completion database rather than administering a single government-run test itself -- in practice a NASBLA-approved vendor's own embedded exam (Boat-Ed, BOATERexam, etc.) IS the de facto qualifying test; this mandate and its scope were independently confirmed by two sources: the Nevada Legislature's own official statute text (leg.state.nv.us/NRS/NRS-488.html), whose NRS 488.730 is titled specifically 'Operation of certain power-driven vessels on INTERSTATE WATERS of State by persons born on or after January 1, 1983,' and Boat-Ed's official Nevada course page (boat-ed.com/nevada), which independently states the same January 1, 1983 birth-date cutoff and >15hp threshold -- the geographic-scope nuance flagged for this build was verified precisely rather than assumed: per NRS 488.035(10), 'interstate waters of this State' means waters forming the boundary between Nevada and an adjoining state, so the statute's letter targets interstate boundary waters specifically rather than being framed as a blanket every-water-body-in-Nevada mandate; a third source, BoatUS Foundation's Nevada boating law summary (boatus.org), independently corroborates both the interstate-waters framing and Nevada's separate 14-year PWC minimum operating age -- because Lake Tahoe (shared with California) and Lake Mead/Lake Mohave and the Colorado River (shared with Arizona) are themselves interstate boundary waters, the mandate's real-world reach covers the large majority of Nevada's actual recreational boating activity even though it is not framed as a universal statewide rule; exam-format convergence is hedged rather than asserted with a false precision: Boat-Ed's Nevada course requires at least 80% on unit quizzes and the final exam with unlimited retake attempts and no minimum age to take the course, but the exact final-exam question count is not consistently published across NDOW-approved vendors and is therefore left unconfirmed; content is also grounded in real Nevada-specific statutory detail independently verified against the Nevada Legislature's own published NRS 488 text: registration/titling via NDOW and a pre-1972 titling exception (NRS 488.065), out-of-state numbering reciprocity (NRS 488.175), fire extinguisher and ventilation-system equipment requirements (NRS 488.193), the 100-foot/200-foot diver's-flag operating restriction (NRS 488.310), the 0.08 BUI blood/breath alcohol standard (NRS 488.400/488.405), aquatic invasive species inspection, impoundment, and decal authority aimed at quagga mussels on Lake Mead and Lake Tahoe (NRS 488.530-488.536), the life-jacket-must-be-worn rule for passengers under 13 (NRS 488.575), reduced-speed and swim-area operating restrictions (NRS 488.600, 488.620), and accident/collision reporting and federal-agency transmittal duties (NRS 488.550, 488.560) -- plus universal NASBLA-aligned boating-safety fundamentals (PFD types, Navigation Rules, the U.S. and Uniform State Aids to Navigation systems, cold-water immersion, and towed water sports) applied to Nevada's uniquely bifurcated boating geography: the low-elevation Mojave Desert heat and monsoon-season dust storms and thunderstorms of Lake Mead and Lake Mohave versus the high-elevation (~6,225 ft), year-round-cold-water alpine conditions of Lake Tahoe -- price matches this project's Motorcycle-tier boating convention ($7.99), not a placeholder
